messages:
jamie.s: Heads-up everyone — we're starting the rollout to deprecate long-lived GitHub PATs for org workflows and move to OIDC / GitHub Apps + short-lived credentials for CI. Main goals: remove secrets from repos, reduce blast radius, and make credential rotation automatic. Timeline: guidance & migration tools out by 2026-04-01, org enforcement (blocks on legacy PAT usage) on 2026-05-15. Please read the plan below and ping if your team needs help.

maria: Quick q — does this affect self-hosted runners?

jamie.s: Yes — self-hosted runners need to support OIDC tokens or use GitHub Apps for auth. For teams using self-hosted + AWS assume-role on runner, switch to OIDC-based role assumption. We'll publish a self-hosted checklist.

sam_k: For infra service accounts (deploy bots) that currently use a PAT in Vault, what's the recommended replacement?

jamie.s: Use a GitHub App with repository-level installation or OIDC with a cloud role. For Vault-stored PATs used by automation, we will provide an adapter that can mint short-lived keys via the GitHub App. We'll run a migration script that opens PRs to replace secrets with a reference to the new credential accessor.

diana: My local dev scripts call the API with my PAT — will devs be forced to rotate or stop using personal tokens?

jamie.s: Personal PATs for interactive dev will remain allowed but we recommend using fine-scoped short-lived tokens (use `gh auth login --web` or `gh auth refresh -s repo`). Org policies only block legacy tokens in workflows and org-level secrets.

maria-devex: Heads-up from devex — we added a CLI check you can run to find PAT usage: `./scripts/find-github-pats.sh` (run from repo root). It scans `.github/workflows` and repo secrets. We'll land an automated PR generator for obvious cases.

jamie.s: Migration notes (short):
- Step 1: enable OIDC trust for your cloud account (AWS/GCP/Azure) and create a role for GitHub OIDC.
- Step 2: update workflows to request `id-token: write` and use an OIDC-aware action or provider. Example snippet: 
```
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v3
- name: Configure cloud creds via OIDC
  uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v2
  with:
    role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsRole
    aws-region: us-west-2
```
- Step 3: remove PATs from repo secrets and update any scripts to call the new short-lived accessor or use the `gh` CLI to fetch tokens.
- Step 4: run the migration checker and open the PRs suggested by the bot.

sam_k: Do we have a way to bulk update org secrets for repos that are hundreds?

jamie.s: Yes — we built a migration tool that can stage PRs across repos and replace secrets with `secrets.GITHUB_APP_TOKEN` references or similar. It requires repo admin consent; devex will coordinate repo owners in a weekly batch.

ops-bot: Automated note — migration-checker job scheduled: weekly-run, next run 2026-03-30 02:00 UTC. Reports will be posted to #eng-security and opened as support tickets for critical repos.

maria: Will we enforce on 2026-05-15 immediately or grace period?

jamie.s: Enforcement policy: on 2026-05-15 we enable org-level SAML/SSO enforcement that blocks legacy PATs in workflows. There will be a 2-week audit window where we only notify owners (May 15–29), then full blocking starts 2026-05-30. We expect most teams to be done well before blocking.

diana: Are there docs & office hours?

jamie.s: Yes — doc: https://intranet.redwood.ai/docs/github-oidc-migration (contains checklist, sample workflows, migration tool usage). Office hours: Tue/Thu 09:00–10:30 PT starting 2026-03-28 in #devex-help. Book a 1:1 with me if you need hands-on migration.

maria: Thanks — we'll run the checker across `platform/*` repos tomorrow and report back.

sam_k: If we hit blockers on org-app install permissions, who to ping?

jamie.s: Ping @jamie.s and @maria or open an internal ticket — include the repo name and the blocker details. We'll escalate to GitHub support if needed.

maria-devex: FYI we'll try to auto-open PRs with the `id-token: write` changes and a README update. PR template will include the migration steps and a CI badge.

jamie.s: One more thing — token-exchange logs will be centrally collected in the Console (Tools -> Auth -> OIDC) so security teams can audit short-lived token minting. If you see unexpected failures after migration, check the logs and file a ticket.

diana: :thumbsup: thanks, team.

maria: Thanks! We'll coordinate and post status updates in this thread.

ops-bot: Ticket created: ENGSEC-4821 "OIDC migration batch: platform/*" assigned to devex.
